q1_what_did_you_play: The whole hand. I led with Rapid Fire so the 3-Spark bank paid for the most expensive card: it prints 2, shows 0, and four hits of 4 into the only enemy on the board is 16 damage for nothing. With the bank spent, Flame on the Wick still costs 0 on its own card, so it went next for 6 more. That left my 2 energy for Kaboom! at its printed cost of 1 (7 damage) and Duck and Cover at 1 for 5 Block. Total 29 damage into Seapunk, leaving it at 16/45, and I eat 6 of the telegraphed 11 instead of the full swing, going to 36 HP.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes — spending the Spark bank on Kaboom! instead of Rapid Fire. That line is Kaboom! at 0, Flame on the Wick at 0, then Rapid Fire at its printed 2, which is the same 29 damage but consumes both energy and leaves nothing for Duck and Cover. Same damage, no Block, so it loses 5 HP for free; the bank should buy the 2-cost, not the 1-cost. I also checked whether dropping Duck and Cover for anything else was possible and it wasn't — there is no fifth card, so the last energy has exactly one use.
q3_what_it_gave_up: Nothing in the hand — every card was played. What it gives up is the ordering risk: I assumed Flame on the Wick, an Attack printed at 0, does not itself eat the Spark bank, so I discharged the bank on Rapid Fire first to make that assumption harmless. It also gives up any notion of holding a card for a later turn; I have no draw or scaling shown, so I took all of it now. And it does not kill — Seapunk lives at 16 with a 45-HP pool, so I have committed my whole hand to a fight I cannot end this turn.
q4_different_intent: Barely. With four cards and no card left unplayable, the hand empties under any telegraph. If Seapunk had shown a block or a buff instead of an 11-damage swing, Duck and Cover would be dead weight — but there is no competing use for that 1 energy, so I would still play it rather than float it. A much larger telegraphed hit would not change it either: 5 Block is the only defense on the page and I already took it. So the intent set the value of the last card, not the choice.
